menuNote: Le Becco dell'Aquila, au-dessus de la vallée de la Sarca
operator: No drop zone: a BASE site, the most jumped exit in the world. The Italian BASE Association keeps the rules (a deployment line for one-piece and wingsuit pilots, ropes on the way down to the exit) and a windsock on the landing field, seen from the exit.

base.name: Becco dell'Aquila
base.evidence: The Italian BASE Association: the Becco dell'Aquila, a natural platform 15 m by 5 m lightly inclined toward the Sarca valley, 1200 m of elevation, the landing field's windsock in sight. OSM puts a node named Becco dell'Aquila in the woods at 45.99385, 10.90442, 1320 m in the LiDAR, with no drop in front of it; 160 m north of it the LiDAR has the rim of the wall, at 1390 m, falling 300 m within 20 m and 440 m within 40 m, both in the 2006-2009 survey and in the 2014 one, and 1175 m above the field. The run starts 12 m back from that rim, down a gentle slope, heading 95 (east), square to the wall; the field is 1.7 km out at 100.

wind.description: The Ora del Garda blows up the valley from the lake, from the south, from late morning, and grows strong by midday: jumps are made early in the morning and late in the afternoon. The Pelèr, from the north, can blow in the morning.

invented: Exit position: the Becco's coordinates are not published and OSM's node has no drop in front of it; the rim used here is the nearest one to it matching the published 1200 m of elevation.
Pattern: inferred from the shape of the valley and the field.
